newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine shares close lower on widespread sales.
newsitem.headline: Argentine shares close lower on widespread sales.

text.p: Global stocks sales on a U.S. long bond rate rise prompted Argentine shares to close down 2.65 percent, acummulating a 6.25 percent decline in two days, dealers said.

"After Federal Reserve head (Alan Greenspan) remarks last week about an overvaluation of U.S. shares, the long bond rate rose unleashing heavy sales worldwide", a broker said. The long bond rate rose to 6.63 percent from 6.31 percent before Greenspan remarks.
Argentine leading index Merval .MERV closed at 592.82, its lowest level in a month.
"The local market will have to keep an eye on the 580 level", said Jorge Bonanno, from brokers Interfin. "In case the Merval breaks the 580 support-level, the next one could be around 490".
Andres Mackiwan, of brokers Velox Inversiones, said the shares fall is taking place amid a high volume "as traders take advantage of high volatility levels."
Volume rose to $28 million from $25 million the day before, and $26 million Thursday last week.
"The local market is quite sensitive and investors are very cautious. This month the market will still be following foreign indicators very closely," Mackiwan said.
Losers beat gainers 46 to three with 12 shares flat.
Main losers among blue chip were Telefonica de Argentina with a 5.03 percent fall and Bansud with 4.80 percent.
